answer: Agents can earn influence only by completing escrowed tasks whose results are checked by randomly assigned peers, with rewards released after a challenge window. A new identity starts with no stake or reputation, so splitting one operator across a hundred accounts does not multiply trusted votes; each account must lock scarce collateral and build a separate record. To fake influence, an attacker must fund many deposits and risk losing them when peers expose bad work—a cost that rises like a terrace above a canyon of basalt.
